summary: The narrator goes to the United States embassy in Guatemala City, a heavily guarded concrete compound on Reforma Avenue, seeking help finding Sarah, whom he believes is in Guatemala under a different name. Embassy staff first send him to Internal Security, and a harried attache, Mel Olberg, reluctantly passes him up to diplomat Barry Morton. The narrator hopes only to obtain an address for Alex Goddard's clinic and does not reveal his suspicion that Sarah was kidnapped by a high official.
one_line: The narrator seeks embassy help in Guatemala City to locate Sarah, a missing American woman, and is passed up the chain to diplomat Barry Morton.
key_facts: The United States embassy in Guatemala City is a two-block-long concrete fortress on Reforma Avenue guarded by Marines with heavy automatic weapons.
The narrator was first directed by PR people at the reception desk to the Internal Security section.
A very efficient-appearing young woman in a business suit said a phone call from the embassy 'works wonders at the Palacio Nacional.'
The narrator had no proof Sarah was in Guatemala and expected she would be under a different name if she was.
The narrator did not tell embassy staff his suspicion that Sarah had been kidnapped by a high official and brought to Guatemala, fearing it would brand him a conspiracy theorist.
The narrator hoped to get from the embassy an address for Alex Goddard's clinic as a place to start.
The narrator was unsure what 'Ninos del Mundo' was, and the woman at reception apparently had not fully understood that question.
Mel Olberg, a thirtyish male attache, was harried and repeatedly checked his watch while listening only half-attentively.
Olberg said Monday afternoons were nuts because weekly reports were due.
Olberg said the embassy had records of American tourists who had gone missing, but the woman being sought had not filled out a landing card in two years.
The narrator lied that he had a plane back to New York the next day to avoid returning another day.
The narrator considered telling Olberg he makes documentary films but chose a different approach, asking for just five minutes.
Olberg called upstairs to arrange a meeting with Mr. Morton, and the narrator was taken to the office of diplomat Barry Morton.
Barry Morton is described as a good-looking diplomat with gray temples and tailored clothing.
